title: Smooth the bumps
story: A transformer gives you a 12 V-peak, 50 Hz sine wave. One diode turns it into bumps that only go positive, but the circuit after it (a 1 kOhm load) needs steady DC. Choose the reservoir capacitor so the output never sags by more than 0.6 V between bumps.

goals.label: output above 10.5 V just before a peak (t = 95 ms)

hints: Between peaks the capacitor alone feeds the load: it loses about I x t / C volts.
The load takes about 11 mA and the gap between peaks is about 20 ms.
Ripple is roughly I / (f x C): solve for C so it stays under 0.6 V.
